item.title: [7] The piezochiral effect
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: A. Cavalleri, P. G. Radaelli

Authors: Z. Zeng, M. Först, M. Fechner, X. Deng, A. Cavalleri, P. G. Radaelli

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Fundamental new strain-responsive functionality controlling chirality in condensed matter.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #material #symmetry #chirality

Abstract: The piezochiral effect, a new member of the family of strain-responsive functionalities alongside piezoelectricity and piezomagnetism, is introduced, enabling control of chirality through mechanical strain, with future applications in photonics, spintronics, biosensing and quantum information.

item.title: [7] Plasmonic metamaterial time crystal
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Marco Schirò, Yannis Laplace

Authors: Tingwen Guo, Jules Sueiro, Gian Marcello Andolina, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental demonstration of a time crystal in a plasmonic metamaterial.

Tags: #metamaterial #timecrystal #plasmonics

Abstract: A plasmonic metamaterial driven at terahertz frequencies achieves strong, ultrafast temporal modulation and shows a transition to the photonic time crystal regime with reduced plasmonic losses.

item.title: [7] Electric dipoles go sideways in thin ferroelectric film
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Elzbieta Gradauskaite

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Fundamental condensed matter physics on ferroelectric thin films.

Tags: #ferroelectrics #thinfilm #materialsphysics

Abstract: Coupling between horizontal and vertical electric polarization enables an unconventional ferroelectric material to be controlled using standard device geometry.
